scope: Source-verified pediatric antibiotic regimens by syndrome
rule: This registry is syndrome- and age-specific. It is not a universal antibiotic table. Selection still requires diagnosis, age, allergy, renal function, culture history and resistance context.

safety_notes.text: This IV arithmetic applies to suspected community-acquired sepsis of unknown focus, age >=28 days and <16 years. A known focus, hospital-acquired infection or ceftriaxone resistance history requires the relevant local antimicrobial pathway. Age 16-17 is outside NG254; use NG253 and indication-specific selection.
Below three calendar months, additional Listeria-active coverage is required by NG254 (for example ampicillin or amoxicillin). This calculator does not select or calculate that companion antibiotic.

At >=50 kg, select the adult regimen for the actual indication and product. A universal 2 g standard / 4 g critical rule is not supported. The automated pediatric calculation stops at 50 kg; no adult dose is inferred.

The NICE lower age limit is 28 days, but the product calcium and bilirubin contraindications include day 28. Premature infants up to postmenstrual age 41 weeks and term neonates <=28 days with hyperbilirubinaemia, jaundice, hypoalbuminaemia or acidosis are contraindicated. Declared postmenstrual age must be consistent with chronological age and birth before 37 completed weeks; inconsistent data require review.

Do not mix or reconstitute with calcium-containing solutions, including Ringer/Hartmann, calcium-containing parenteral nutrition or IV calcium salts. No simultaneous administration, including same-line/Y connections; different lines or sites alone do not remove the general prohibition. Neonates <=28 days needing or expected to need IV calcium are contraindicated even with separation. Above 28 days, sequential administration requires the specified separate/replaced/flushed lines. The label exception for continuous calcium-containing parenteral nutrition via different lines and different sites is expert-only and remains outside this automated module.

This sepsis entry is IV only. Ceftriaxone prepared with lidocaine must never be administered IV. For a separately indicated IM regimen, do not exceed 1 g per site; a 2 g IM dose requires separate sites. Reconstitution volume/concentration and lidocaine contraindications are product-specific. 3.5 mL can be the added solvent volume and is not a universal final-volume cap.

Isolated renal impairment with preserved hepatic function generally needs no routine reduction, but CrCl <10 mL/min carries a 2 g/day label ceiling and requires regimen review here. Mild/moderate isolated hepatic impairment with preserved renal function generally needs no adjustment; evidence is insufficient for severe hepatic impairment. Severe combined renal/hepatic impairment requires close monitoring and individual review, not an inferred universal 2 g rule.

A returned number is source-linked arithmetic, not prescribing clearance. Allergy, exact product, local protocol, administration conditions and clinical response remain subject to clinician/pharmacy review. No product stock, compatibility for an unlisted mixture or prospective clinical validation is inferred.
